question: How does ValidationPipe + class-validator validate bodies?
shortAnswer: Transforms plain objects to DTO classes then runs decorators; throws BadRequest on failures.
detailedAnswer: Requires transform for nested types. Customize exceptionFactory for error shape.

question: Validate nested arrays of objects — requirements?
shortAnswer: @ValidateNested({ each: true }) and @Type(() => ItemDto) with transform enabled.
detailedAnswer: Missing @Type is the most common bug. Add unit tests for nested payloads.

question: Custom validators — when?
shortAnswer: Cross-field rules, DB uniqueness checks (carefully), or domain formats not covered by built-ins.
detailedAnswer: Prefer sync validators in pipes; async uniqueness often better in services to keep pipes pure.

question: Zod/io-ts vs class-validator in Nest — trade-offs?
shortAnswer: Zod offers TS-first inference; class-validator is decorator-native to Nest examples and Swagger plugins.
detailedAnswer: Either works — consistency matters. Nest pipes can adapt Zod schemas.

question: Scenario: validation passes but business rule fails later.
shortAnswer: Input validation is not domain invariants — enforce invariants in domain services and map to 422/409.
detailedAnswer: Don't overload DTOs with all business rules. Keep boundaries clear.

question: Lead: org-wide validation standards for Nest APIs?
shortAnswer: Global pipe config, shared error format, security defaults (whitelist), and linters for DTO coverage.
detailedAnswer: Security review for file uploads and string lengths. Fuzz critical parsers.
